name: python-web
description: A Python web application (for example FastAPI, Django or Flask) that serves an API and, often, a built single-page-app frontend from one process.

runtimes.version: <from pyproject.toml's requires-python, or a pinned version file>
runtimes.provision: <installed on dev and prod hosts; a per-app virtual environment>

runtimes.version: <from the frontend's package.json engines field, if a frontend is built>
runtimes.provision: <installed on hosts that build the frontend; not needed at runtime>

build.what: Frontend bundle, if the app serves one

services.start: <e.g. a uvicorn/gunicorn command, or the framework's own server run behind a real process manager>
services.manager: <a service manager or a container runtime>
services.bind: <loopback-only, unless a trusted edge forwards identity>

config.rule: kept out of version control; seeded from a committed example file; real values set by hand per environment

data.migrations: <the app's migration tool, e.g. alembic or Django migrations>
data.state: <an external database; nothing durable lives on the app host itself>

verify: the health endpoint returns a body with a status field, not just HTTP 200
a rendered page or the frontend bundle's hash changed, so an old bundle behind a new backend cannot pass
